name: Free Flow of Non-Personal Data Regulation
evidence_rating: thin: no promised indicators measured; evaluation evidence qualitative and points to limited effect; no causal studies
summary: The Commission expected the Regulation to add up to EUR 8 billion a year to EU GDP by removing national rules on where data must be stored. That gain was never measured; an evaluation study and the Commission's own 2025 review found limited uptake, no recorded use of its enforcement mechanisms and little success in removing localisation rules. The Commission now proposes to repeal it and move its core principle into the Data Act.

indicators.objective: The proposal's financial statement has no indicators section; the memorandum promised an evaluation five years on using indicators from the impact assessment, Eurostat and DESI data

indicators.indicator: Reduction in the number and range of data localisation restrictions
indicators.evidence: Not quantified. The 2026 evaluation support study finds limited effectiveness in removing localisation requirements, hampered by the national-security exemption and uncertainty about mixed data sets.

indicators.indicator: Member States can access data stored abroad for regulatory control
indicators.evidence: No publicly reported cases under the Article 5 cooperation or penalty mechanisms; authorities report low demand.

indicators.indicator: Better transparency on conditions for data porting (self-regulatory codes)
indicators.evidence: Codes of conduct had limited uptake and were superseded by binding switching rules in the Data Act (2023); Commission calls Article 6 practically obsolete.

indicators.indicator: Trust in free flow of non-personal data
indicators.evidence: Consultation: fewer than 4 in 10 respondents see any objective fully met; weakest scores on trust/security and switching; about half have little or no familiarity with the Regulation.

indicators.indicator: GDP gain of up to EUR 8bn a year (0.06% of GDP) from removing localisation restrictions

literature.citation: European Commission (2017), Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal on a framework for the free flow of non-personal data (executive summary SWD(2017) 305), SWD(2017) 304
literature.title: Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal on a framework for the free flow of non-personal data (executive summary SWD(2017) 305)
literature.method: ex-ante (relies on ECIPE and Deloitte modelling)
literature.headline: Removing localisation restrictions could raise GDP by up to EUR 8bn (0.06%) a year (ECIPE); Deloitte estimate of EUR 11.6bn net present value for cloud users and providers; moderate costs for cloud providers
literature.summary_plain: The Commission expected that banning unjustified national rules on where data must be stored would add up to EUR 8 billion a year to EU GDP.

literature.citation: Bauer, Ferracane, Lee-Makiyama & van der Marel (2016), Unleashing Internal Data Flows in the EU: An Economic Assessment of Data Localisation Measures in the EU Member States, ECIPE Policy Brief 3/2016
literature.authors: Bauer, Ferracane, Lee-Makiyama & van der Marel
literature.title: Unleashing Internal Data Flows in the EU: An Economic Assessment of Data Localisation Measures in the EU Member States
literature.headline: Identified 22 localisation measures in EU Member States; removing them would raise GDP by up to EUR 8bn a year (0.06%)
literature.summary_plain: A think-tank model found 22 national data localisation rules in the EU and estimated that scrapping them could add up to EUR 8 billion a year to GDP.

literature.authors: Open Evidence et al. for the European Commission
literature.title: Study supporting the evaluation of the free flow of non-personal data regulation, open data directive and data governance act
literature.headline: Regulation has shown limited effectiveness in removing data localisation requirements, hampered by the national-security exemption and legal uncertainty about mixed data sets
literature.summary_plain: An evaluation study for the Commission concluded the Regulation did little to remove national data localisation rules.

literature.citation: European Commission (2025), Staff working document accompanying the Digital Omnibus proposals, SWD(2025) 836
literature.title: Staff working document accompanying the Digital Omnibus proposals
literature.headline: Limited uptake and modest stakeholder interest; no publicly reported cases under cooperation or penalty mechanisms; switching codes superseded by the Data Act; fewer than 4 in 10 consultation respondents see any objective fully met; proposes repealing the Regulation and moving the free-flow principle into the Data Act
literature.summary_plain: The Commission found little use of the Regulation and proposes folding its core principle into the Data Act and repealing it.
